name: alert-dialog
title: Alert Dialog
description: A modal dialog that interrupts the user with important content and expects a response.
usageSnippet:
<AlertDialog>
  <@trigger|props|>
    <Button ...props variant="outline">Show Dialog</Button>
  </@trigger>
  <@title>Are you absolutely sure?</@title>
  <@description>
    This action cannot be undone.
  </@description>
</AlertDialog>

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Human readable label for the dialog, in event the dialog title is not rendered

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Whether to close the dialog when the escape key is pressed

props.name: closeOnInteractOutside
props.description: Whether to close the dialog when the outside is clicked

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
The initial open state of the dialog when rendered.
Use when you don't need to control the open state of the dialog.

props.name: defaultTriggerValue
props.description:
The initial active trigger value when rendered.
Use when you don't need to control the active trigger value.

props.name: finalFocusEl
props.description: Element to receive focus when the dialog is closed

props.name: getRootNode
props.description: A root node to correctly resolve document in custom environments. E.x.: Iframes, Electron.

props.name: ids
props.description: The ids of the elements in the dialog. Useful for composition.

props.name: initialFocusEl
props.description: Element to receive focus when the dialog is opened

props.name: modal
props.description: Whether to prevent pointer interaction outside the element and hide all content below it

props.name: open
props.description: The controlled open state of the dialog

props.name: persistentElements
props.description:
Returns the persistent elements that:
- should not have pointer-events disabled
- should not trigger the dismiss event

props.name: preventScroll
props.description: Whether to prevent scrolling behind the dialog when it's opened

props.name: restoreFocus
props.description: Whether to restore focus to the element that had focus before the dialog was opened

props.name: trapFocus
props.description: Whether to trap focus inside the dialog when it's opened

events.name: onEscapeKeyDown
events.description: Function called when the escape key is pressed

events.name: onFocusOutside
events.description: Function called when the focus is moved outside the component

events.name: onInteractOutside
events.description: Function called when an interaction happens outside the component

events.name: onOpenChange
events.description: Function to call when the dialog's open state changes

events.name: onPointerDownOutside
events.description: Function called when the pointer is pressed down outside the component

events.name: onRequestDismiss
events.description: Function called when this layer is closed due to a parent layer being closed

events.name: onTriggerValueChange
events.description: Function to call when the active trigger changes

accessibilityNotes: Rendered with `role="alertdialog"` (not `"dialog"`) so assistive technology announces it as requiring an explicit response, per the [WAI-ARIA Alert and Message Dialogs Pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/).
Focus moves into the dialog on open and is trapped there until it closes; it's restored to the trigger element on close.

Unlike a plain dialog, closing via the Escape key and clicking outside the content are both disabled by default (`closeOnEscape={false}`, `closeOnInteractOutside={false}`) — the user must choose Cancel or Continue.
The title and description are linked to the content via `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`, generated automatically from `@title`/`@description`.

examples.title: Basic
examples.source:
import AlertDialog from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/alert-dialog/alert-dialog.marko";
import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";

<AlertDialog>
  <@trigger|props|>
    <Button type="button" ...props variant="outline">Show Dialog</Button>
  </@trigger>
  <@title>Are you absolutely sure?</@title>
  <@description>
    This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete your account and remove your data from our servers.
  </@description>
</AlertDialog>
examples.description: A basic alert dialog with a title, description, and cancel and continue buttons.

examples.title: Small
examples.source:
import AlertDialog from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/alert-dialog/alert-dialog.marko";
import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";

<AlertDialog size="sm" cancelText="Don't allow" actionText="Allow">
  <@trigger|props|>
    <Button type="button" ...props variant="outline">Show Dialog</Button>
  </@trigger>
  <@title>Allow accessory to connect?</@title>
  <@description>
    Do you want to allow the USB accessory to connect to this device?
  </@description>
</AlertDialog>
examples.description: Use the `size="sm"` prop to make the alert dialog smaller.

examples.title: Media
examples.source:
import AlertDialog from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/alert-dialog/alert-dialog.marko";
import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";
import Icon from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/icon/icon.marko";

<AlertDialog cancelText="Cancel" actionText="Share">
  <@trigger|props|>
    <Button type="button" ...props variant="outline">Share Project</Button>
  </@trigger>
  <@media>
    <Icon name="CirclePlusIcon"/>
  </@media>
  <@title>Share this project?</@title>
  <@description>
    Anyone with the link will be able to view and edit this project.
  </@description>
</AlertDialog>
examples.description: Use the `@media` slot to add a media element such as an icon or image to the alert dialog.

examples.title: Destructive
examples.source:
import AlertDialog from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/alert-dialog/alert-dialog.marko";
import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";

<AlertDialog
  cancelText="No, keep it"
  actionText="Yes, delete it"
  action=() => { console.log("deleted"); }
>
  <@trigger|props|>
    <Button type="button" ...props variant="destructive">Delete account</Button>
  </@trigger>
  <@title>Delete account</@title>
  <@description>
    This will permanently delete your account. This action is irreversible.
  </@description>
</AlertDialog>
examples.description: Override `cancelText` and `actionText`, and run side effects on confirm with the `action` callback.

examples.description: The `dir` prop is a native attribute pass-through — set it on `<AlertDialog>` to flip logical-property layout and typography for right-to-left languages. Every RTL example on this site does it the same way: a `dir="rtl"` wrapper plus Arabic labels.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.source:
import AlertDialog from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/alert-dialog/alert-dialog.marko"; import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";
{ open = o; }> <@trigger|props|> <@title>Controlled alert dialog <@description>The open state is controlled by the parent component. open: ${String(open)}
examples.description: Zag machines are controlled: an `open` prop without a change handler never moves. Pair it with `openChange`, or use Marko's bind shorthand `open:=state`.

composition: `<AlertDialog>` is one file exposing upstream's tree as slots: `@trigger` (render-prop, receives the trigger props to spread onto your own element — never nest a `<button>` inside it), `@media` (optional icon/image above the title), `@title`, and `@description`. The footer's Cancel/Continue buttons are generated from props (`cancelText`/`actionText`, `cancelVariant`/`actionVariant`, `action`) rather than composed as separate slots.
